0.name: data
0.description: Streamed TDM frames; 'length' in the wire header [type:u16][length:u16] is the number of repeats of this field group. One repeat = one FRAME: a timestamp followed by one sample per channel. Slots are 32 bits (not 16 as in sizif): a uint16 timestamp wraps every 32 s at 2048 Hz, and real EEG front-ends such as the TI ADS1299 are 24-bit, which 16-bit slots would throw away. All slots share one width because the PL filter is time-division multiplexed -- one slot per clock, slot 0 passing through unfiltered. Adding a channel means adding a chN field here; that regenerates the C header and the numpy dtypes together. NOTE: the DMA buffer must be a whole number of frames AND a multiple of 32 bytes for cache maintenance; 8 frames satisfies both for any channel count, so keep the per-packet frame count a multiple of 8.

1.name: config
1.description: Filter configuration, PC <-> board, same layout in both directions. op=0 READ: the board ignores every other field and replies with its current registers. op=1 WRITE: the board applies n_channels/shift/ctrl and then replies the same way. The reply is always a read-back of the actual hardware registers, never an echo of what was asked for, so a value the fabric clamped or ignored shows up as a mismatch instead of being invisible. status is read-only (the filter's STATUS word) and is ignored on the way in. log_mask is the board's UART verbosity (COMM_LOG_* bits in comm_log.h); it is a firmware setting rather than a fabric register, but it rides here because it is the same thing: a runtime parameter you set and read back.

2.name: metrics
2.description: Board health, pushed once per second, board -> PC only. The PC never sends this and the board never expects a reply. Same numbers the [S] console line prints, so the serial console and the GUI can never disagree -- both are built from one computation in main.c. Every rate is normalized by window_ms rather than assumed to be exactly 1000 ms, because the stats check runs once per main-loop pass and the window always overshoots slightly. lat_*_us is BOARD-SIDE service latency -- a complete packet in the rx ring to its echo handed to lwIP -- not end-to-end round trip. End-to-end would be dominated by the PC's scheduler, the relay and TCP, none of which this architecture controls; this isolates the part DMA was meant to make deterministic. Jitter is lat_max_us - lat_min_us. All zero means no packets were serviced in the window.
